about: The Marvel Super Heroes sourcebooks this repo reads, one entry per book, keyed by slug.
Marvel's own registry: scripts/books.json is the Palladium books' and is not read or written by anything in scripts/msh/.
title, short    the book's name, and the code a card cites it by (MA1)
ORDER MATTERS: the first book here keeps plain ids (magneto); every later one's ids end in -<slug> (magneto-mhsp1), so no two books collide and no id depends on build order
source_pdf, source_pdf_dir  where scripts/msh/ocr-book.py reads the scan from
sha256          of that PDF, so a different scan of the same book is noticed
pdf_pages       the PDF's page count; the OCR cache names pages p001..pNNN by PDF page
offset          printed page = PDF page - offset
offset_evidence how the offset was measured
columns         text columns on a body page
stat_labels     the four secondary values printed beside the FASERIP grid, in the book's spelling
section_labels  the run-in headings that divide an entry, in the book's spelling
rank_aliases    rank codes as this book prints them -> apps/marvel-heroes/data/ranks.json ids, misprints included
sections        the printed Contents: [section, subsection or null, printed first page]
contents_errata where the Contents and the pages disagree: {section, contents_page, page, note}; the page wins
character_pages the printed range scripts/msh/roster.py reads for characters; the rest of the book is items and an adventure
item_pages      the printed range scripts/msh/extras.py reads for items and locations
item_parts      run-in names that are PARTS of an item or location, not new ones (the Danger Room's event kinds)

adventure       the book's adventure: its title and printed range, for scripts/msh/extras.py; the maps after it are not text. Adventures are not in the app (2026-09-29): extras.py parses one only for the items found inside it, so only MHSP1 has one, and a new book leaves this out
index           the printed index: [name, [printed pages]], transcribed and checked against the page images

parts           a boxed module of several booklets, each numbered from 1: {name, cite (the booklet as a card cites it), pdf: [first, last], offset or null}; replaces offset, which assumes one numbering

layout          how the character pages are set: absent for MA1's (scripts/msh/roster.py); roster-booklet for MHSP1's (scripts/msh/booklet.py); grid-booklets for ME1's, MA1's grids in a boxed module (scripts/msh/gridbooks.py)
character_ranges  a grid-booklets book: [{part, pages: [first, last] printed}] that scripts/msh/gridbooks.py reads for characters
opponents       a grid-booklets book: adventure pages that stat a character inside their prose, {part, page, names}; an entry there ends where the prose resumes
roster_sections Contents sections whose sub-entries are characters, a checklist every name of which must be found
tiers           statted generic types the Contents does not list by that name (Typical Skrull Warrior), a checklist too
teams           [part, first printed page, team]: the team of an entry is the last one at or before its first page
character_part  with parts: the booklet character_pages counts in
item_part       with parts: the booklet item_pages counts in

locations       a roster-booklet book's locations: {name, section (the adventure section that describes it), parts, part_aliases, items (run-ins inside it that are items), rooms (its room table: columns, and rows of [sector, d100 range, a room per column], transcribed by eye)}
vehicles        vehicles a roster-booklet book states inside an adventure section: {name, section}; control, speed and body are read from that section

adventure_tables  tables inside adventure sections that the column cut cannot read as prose: {section, pdf, box (TSV pixels) cut out of the text, note}. Only the box is read: the adventure is not in the app, so no table is carried as data

adventure.sections  a roster-booklet book's adventure, in page order: [kind, title, how its first line reads, extra]; kind setting, planned (the third field is its day and shift, and a fourth its first words where OCR lost its title), random (extra: its roll, and "once"), location, or skip (running notes, which are on the characters)
one_line_tiers  one-line blocks that are beings of their own, not a form of the character (Klaw's sound creatures)
running         a booklet of running notes, one per character: {part, pages, aliases: {name as the note prints it: entry header}}
reference_summary a chart of every character's ranks, Health and Karma: {pdf, heroes, villains}, rows [name, "F A S E R I P" as printed, Health, Karma, [powers]], transcribed by eye
sections (with parts) a fourth field names the booklet whose Contents lists the entry, since each booklet numbers from 1 (ME1)

reference_summary rows may give the seven ranks as a list of the printed values, number and code, where the chart prints both (ME1); a grid-booklets book's chart names its part and the team its chart-only heroes join
layout code-grids for MA4's grids, whose rows print the code before the number ("F GD (10)"): scripts/msh/codegrids.py

headings        a code-grids book: [printed page, TITLE] titles that are not characters (a race, a place, a group); each opens a heading entry and must be found once. ' / ' joins a title set on two lines. A third field names the tier its run-ins are members of (NOTABLE SKRULLS: SKRULL)
item_headers    a code-grids book: [printed page, TITLE, location|vehicle] for each place and vehicle scripts/msh/extras.py reads in item_pages, matched once in capitals
grid_headers    a code-grids book: [printed page, Health, NAME] for a character header the OCR lost; a line with the name goes in above that grid
block_labels    a code-grids book: [printed page, Health, label] for a grid that is a form or an item inside another entry (The Thing's Human Form); it gets no header of its own
statted_pages   a code-grids book: pages outside character_pages that stat beings inside a place's text, {page, team (the place), names, partial: [[NAME, Karma]] for a grid printing only R, I and P}
teams (code-grids) [printed page, first entry's header, team] in book order: each starts a run of that team
team_names      a roster-book book: {team as its banner prints it: the team its cards file under}; an entry under no banner files under the book's title

layout cover-panels for MH1's: MHSP1's blocks on a loose cover's inside panels and a few booklet pages, with one-line grids in the chapters (scripts/msh/coverpanels.py). It reads character_ranges and opponents in ME1's form, and:
panels          a cover-panels book: parts (offset null, no printed page) read whole for cards; a card there cites the panel
cards           a cover-panels book: [part, printed page or null, name] for every full block, read off the page images; with opponents, the checklist
not_characters  a cover-panels book: card headers that are not characters (a vehicle), dropped
no_health       a cover-panels book: opponents whose one-line grid prints no Health; scripts/msh/npcs.py gives each F+A+S+E, flagged health_derived

no_karma        a cover-panels book: opponents whose one-line grid prints no Karma and a ruling derives it; scripts/msh/npcs.py gives each R+I+P, flagged karma_derived (MH2's Kang's Minions), or whose full block prints the word none (MH3's Miss Locke and Mr. Chambers). Absent, an unprinted Karma stays null
teams (cover-panels) {team: [names]}: a character named there is that team's; every other files under the book's title
faint_rules     a cover-panels book: [part, printed page, y in TSV pixels]: a rule between two cards that booklet.rules() cannot see (a dashed one)
drop_above      a cover-panels book: [part, printed page, y in TSV pixels]: text above y on that page is not a card's (the Epilog over Magneto's)
drop_corner     a cover-panels book: [part, printed page, x, y in TSV pixels]: every word right of x and below y on that page is not a card's (MH2's PROOF OF PURCHASE coupon)

opponent_names  a cover-panels book: "title" where a one-line grid's name is in title case, alone on the line above it (MH2's "Aliens (humanoid)"); its run-in powers after the Powers: line are read as a card's are. Absent, MH1's capitals
form_grids      a cover-panels book: [{part, page, entry, label}]: a one-line grid with no name above it that is a second block on that card (MH2's Mimic, once he has copied the Avengers' powers)

opponent_powers a cover-panels book: "run-in" where a one-line grid's Powers: line is followed by run-in powers in capitals (MH3's "WEAPONS: Each tower", "FLIGHT is at good speed."), read as its powers, going on at the top of the next column on a run-in line; a stat line opening a bracket it does not close keeps its number and sends the bracket to prose. Absent, MH1's
drop_lines      a cover-panels book: [part, printed page or null, text]: a line that is no card's text, matched once whole (MH3's In Loving Memory banner over Doom's card)

lost_headers    a cover-panels book: [part, printed page or null, identity line, NAME]: a card header no word of the TSV holds (MH3's Human Torch); a header line with the name goes in above that identity line

moves           a cover-panels book: [part, printed page, col, y from, y to, after col, after y in TSV pixels]: the lines of that column between those heights go on after the last line of the other column ending above that height (MH3's Super-Adaptoid, its text set round its portrait)
card_grids      a cover-panels book: [{part, page or null, entry, label}]: a one-line grid inside that card's text, a second block on it with that label (MH3's She-Hulk and Thing, their human forms)

prose_cards     a cover-panels book: [{part, page, name}]: a full block set inside a chapter's prose (MH4's Kingpin, printed 5), headed by its name in title case on a line of its own, which the header test does not take; read as a card from that line to the next header or one-line grid

unnamed_grids   a cover-panels book: [{part, page, name}], in page order: a one-line grid with no name line above it that is a character of its own, named by what the page's prose calls it (MH4's Reggie and Cyber-Sergeants). form_grids is for one that is a form of a card

split_headers   a cover-panels book: [part, printed page or null, as read, NAME]: a card header Tesseract read as two words (MH4's TASKMASTE R, split at the trademark sign), matched once by its cleaned text and joined

repeat_grids    a cover-panels book: [{part, page, name, of}]: a one-line grid that repeats another entry's grid (MH4's 2 Minions on printed 12 and 13, Modok's Minions'); scripts/msh/coverpanels.py checks its codes, Health and Karma against that entry's and it is not an entry (survey mh4.md decision 6)

section_labels (cover-panels) a label beyond Powers, Talents and Background is a section too (MH4's Important People and Equipment), keyed in lower case with underscores (important_people); a run-in under Equipment is read as a power is and carries section: equipment. A count before a one-line grid's name (2 Panthers) and a Special: value on its Health line (Health: 60 Special: Claws, the Special a power named as printed) are read without a field

panel_foot      a cover-panels book: true where a panel's columns run below the foot a folio page keeps (95.5% of the height), so scripts/msh/coverpanels.py reads the lines there too (MH4; MH1-3 print nothing there)

card_names      {name the card would be built with: card name}: scripts/msh/npcs.py names that card, and its id and its version's id follow the new name; for two books' different people who print one name (MA1's and MH1's Ariel, Nate 2026-10-21). Each must find exactly one entry with no parenthesis in its header. Absent, a card is named as built
grid_headers (grid-booklets) [{part, page, health, name}] for a character header the OCR lost (ME2's BALDER): a line with the name goes in above the grid printing that Health

one_line_grids  a grid-booklets book: one-line grids (letters, numbers, codes, then Health and Karma; ME2), in reading order per page: {part, page, name} for a character of its own with no header (the chapter's prose names it), or {part, page, entry, label} for a form inside that entry. teams may be left out until they are decided; an entry then has none

second_blocks   a grid-booklets book: [{part, page, name, label}]: a one_line_grids character that is a second block on the card of that name in another booklet (ME2's Titans and Zeus in Hades), labelled, its run-in powers going to D1 as the card's (scripts/msh/npcs.py)

rank_ranges     true: scripts/msh/roster.py's check passes a number anywhere inside its rank's range (apps/marvel-heroes/data/ranks.json min and max), not only the standard number (ME2, Nate 2026-10-21). Absent, a number must be its rank's standard or an override must say why
The cache is under WORKSHOP_MSH_CACHE (default .cache/msh), never committed. The survey is apps/marvel-heroes/docs/surveys/<slug>.md.
